title: Per-route timeout mosaics and socket stewardship for cross-language SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Ship a cross-SDK feature set and examples that let app developers express per-route timeout mosaics (distinct deadline/idle/stream timeouts by priority lane), adaptive connection-pooling/keepalive hints, and streaming ergonomics that avoid head-of-line blocking. Deliverables: 1) API surface additions in Python/TS/Go for per-route timeout profiles and a 'socket stewardship' config object; 2) reference examples (quickstart) showing low-latency single-turn, streaming with reconnection/backpressure, and high-throughput batching with pooled sockets; 3) telemetry events and doc pages describing recommended presets for latency-sensitive vs throughput-sensitive routes; 4) unit/integration tests and a migration guide for existing clients.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a per-route config that accepts: deadline_ms, idle_stream_ms, conn_keepalive_ms, max_idle_connections, priority (low/normal/high)
SDKs provide a language-consistent 'StewardConfig' (name may vary) with sensible defaults and an escape hatch for raw transport knobs

Three cross-language quickstarts (python/ts/go) are published and linked from the SDK docs demonstrating: short-deadline single-turn, streaming with graceful reconnect and resume, and high-throughput reuse with prefix caching
E2E benchmarks show <=5% median latency regression for default config and >=20% cost savings for throughput profile in our benchmark harness
Telemetry events emitted for pool saturation, connection churn, reconnects, and stream resume that feed the Console dashboard
Backward-compatible: existing clients keep current behavior unless they opt-in to new profiles
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting — aligned on API shapes across languages. Agreed to call the top-level config 'steward_config' and expose per-route 'timeout_profile'.
2026-02-24: Design doc posted (link below). Initial TypeScript surface drafted; Python/Go shapes derived and reviewed by SDK leads.

2026-02-27: Bench harness added a new workload simulating mixed short-chat + long-stream traffic. Early runs show uncontrolled keepalive churn for the throughput profile — investigating pooling heuristics.
2026-03-02: Implemented adaptive conn prune: pool prunes connections if idle for conn_keepalive_ms * 2 and if pool size > max_idle_connections. Added metrics for conn_reaped and pool_gc_runs.
2026-03-04: First PRs opened: TS (#5890), Python (#5891), Go (#5892). TS and Python build green; Go test flake on streaming resume handled in follow-up.
